question.text: This is the total number of women who have ever been Supreme Court justices, past and present.
question.clue: This number of emperors who ruled after the imposition of the Tetrarchy system by Diocletian.

swap.leadin: Since 2012, part of this body of water has been officially defined by a bordering nation as the "West Philippine Sea."
swap.text: Name this sea, a section of the Pacific Ocean, where the Nine-Dash Line marks a major territory claim.
swap.answerHtml: South China Sea (accept Nan Hai or Nan Zhongguo Hai)

question.leadin: Answer these questions about pivotal events in the People's Republic of China.
question.text: Prior to the Long March, this man regained power at the Zunyi Conference; he later declared the establishment of the People's Republic of China at Tian'anmen Square.
question.clue: His Red Army evacuated through the Long March before eventually driving the Kuomintang out of mainland China.

swap.leadin: The Kashag was the governing council of Tibet during this dynasty and its independent period.
swap.text: Name this dynasty led by the House of Aisin-Gioro. This Manchu-led dynasty was the last dynasty of China.
swap.answerHtml: Qing Dynasty [or the Great Qing or Qīng cháo or Dà Qīng]
swap.clue: The longest ruling Chinese Emperor was from this dynasty.

question.leadin: This rebellion was partially sparked by a severe two-year-long drought in the Shan-dong.
question.text: Name this 1899-1901 rebellion against western influence, which was led by the Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists.
question.clue: The Seymour and Gaselee expeditions aimed to reach the besieged Legation Quarter during this event.

swap.text: The Zhou dynasty succeeded the Shang, and the first half of its "Eastern" period is known by this name. The seasonal name for this period is taken from the title of the official chronicle of the Lu dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Spring and Autumn Period (accept Spring and Autumn Annals; accept Chun qiu shi chi)
swap.clue: That royal family's flight from Zongzhou to Chengzhou initiated this time period, which the rise of the states of Wu and Yue.

question.text: The kingdom of Wei was founded by this man's son, Pi. This warlord won the Battle of Guandu, and served as the chancellor to the last Han emperor.
question.clue: This man originally rose to power as a Chancellor of the Eastern Han dynasty in its waning days.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous bridges in Chinese history.
swap.text: During this event, Edgar Snow recounts how soldiers bravely crossed the Luding chain bridge under machine gun fire and defeated their opponents. This event took place following the Fifth Encirclement Campaign.
swap.clue: The Fifth Encirclement forced this event, which Otto Braun took part in. The participants of this event defeated warlord forces at the Battle of Luding Bridge and reshuffled their leadership at the Zunyi Conference.

question.text: Deng presided over the handover of this British colony to China by promising "One Country, Two Systems" to maintain this colony's existing administrative system.
question.answerHtml: Hong Kong [or Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China]
question.clue: At that time, this polity was restored to its previous owner, who had this polity ceded to them in 1842 after the First Opium War.

swap.leadin: It fixed the approximate boundries of China and established the first great Chinese empire.
swap.text: Identify this dynasty that began construction of the Great Wall and burned books in order to eliminate competing philosophies of rule.
swap.clue: Despite claims in Records of the Grand Historian, this dynasty most likely did not "bury the Confucians" during a book burning.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the United States' involvement in China during World War II.
question.text: Claire Lee Chennault led the American Volunteer Group, a volunteer air force in China during World War II that is usually referred to by this two-word English nickname.
question.clue: The plan to create this group was put forth by its leader's press officer Joseph Alsop, and approved after a lengthy debate at the Trident Conference, to the dismay of a man known as "Vinegar Joe," Joseph Stilwell.

swap.leadin: Nationalism, democracy, and welfare were this man's "Three Principles of the People."
swap.text: Name this leader who inspired the overthrow of the Qing Dynasty in 1911 and served as the first President of the Republic of China.
swap.answerHtml: Sun Yat-sen [or Sun Zhongshan; or Sun Yixian; prompt on Yat-sen]
swap.clue: A Christian educated in Hawaii, he founded the Whampoa Military Academy, which trained those who undertook the Northern Expedition.

question.leadin: This city names a "golden decade" of economic growth after the Warlord Era whic ended with its swift capture during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
question.text: Name this city, which became capital of the Nationalist Republic of China in 1927 under Chiang Kai-Shek.
question.clue: This city surrendered to the Manchu without a siege during the Fall of the Ming Dynasty, and one treaty named for this city was signed aboard the HMS Cornwallis, and ended the Thirteen Factories system.

swap.leadin: The Cheng Wu manuscript describes a dream of this dynasty's queen Tai Si foretelling their victory over their predecessors.
swap.text: Name this dynasty established after its predecessors were defeated at the Battle of Muye. The Five Classics, including the I Ching, are traditionally thought to have been written during this dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Zhōu (“joe”) dynasty [or Zhōu Cháo; accept Eastern Zhōu or Western Zhōu or Xīzhōu or Dōngzhōu]
swap.clue: Wu was also the son of King Weng, who is credited with being this dynasty's first emperor.

question.leadin: A jinshi jidi was a person who excelled at the highest level in this procedure through their mastery of Confucian texts.
question.text: Name this institution of imperial China from the Tang dynasty well into the 1800s, which was praised for meritocratically selecting candidates for the bureaucracy.

swap.leadin: Some of these people became idolized by the peasantry after they moved to the countryside and founded seowon ("SUH-wun").
swap.text: Name this class of people who staffed the Hall of Worthies. A "forest" of these people formed the Sarim faction before they were purged by the Hungu.
swap.answerHtml: scholars [or seonbi; or literati; or academics; prompt on officials or bureaucrats or ministers or civil servants]
swap.clue: The intensive preparation needed to become one of these people by undertaking the Gwageo meant most were also a yangban.

question.leadin: Name these incidents in the run-up to World War II in Asia.
question.text: In 1915, Japan had secured control of its territorial interests in China with this document that Yuan Shikai signed. Due to its rejection of the Open Door Policy, this document was modified in the Lansing-Ishii agreement.

swap.leadin: Excavations at these people's tomb in Tuerji Mountain uncovered the remains of a priestess wearing a golden headdress and bells on her ankles.
swap.text: Name these people, whose leader Yelu Deguang established the Liao dynasty after capturing Kaifeng. In the 600s, these people formed the Dahe Confederacy to resist Tang rule.
swap.clue: They divided their holdings into the Northern and Southern Chancellories and their emperors included men such as Shengzong and Jingzong, while their first ruler took the name Taizu and was known as Abaoji.

question.text: This Tang princess was married off to Songtsen Gampo, the founder of the Tibetan Empire. She is traditionally credited with introducing Chinese agriculture, porcelain, and other innovations to Tibetan culture.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about "poet-historians" in Chinese history.
swap.text: Du Fu is often considered one of the foremost poet-historians since his poems, such as "Lament by the Riverside," depict the sorrows of this political revolt instigated by a Sogdian, Turkic general.
